own_scenes.family: Costa Oeste: Los Ángeles, Compton, la Bahía
own_scenes.desc: La bahía, lejos de los grandes mercados como el Sur, tuvo una escena independiente de «hazlo tú mismo»: Todd Shaw, llegado de Los Ángeles, vendía cintas a medida con Freddy B y desde el maletero; los camellos se pasaban sus cintas. Con Don’t Stop Rappin’ (1983) en su sello 75 Girls, «Shortrapp» y «Girl (Cocaine)» hablaba sucio de cocaína, chulos y «bitches» antes de N.W.A o Ice-T. Jive reeditó Born to Mack (1988), con «Freaky Tales»: las fábricas de prensado se negaban, no sonó en radio y llegó al platino, primero en el Sur. Ant Banks, que aprendía Parliament en un Casio, vendía cintas con MC Ant; con Too $hort montó la Dangerous Crew, músicos de funk (Shorty B, Sean G, Pee Wee) y raperos (Dangerous Dame, Spice 1, Rappin’ Ron), y Shorty the Pimp (1992). Quería hacer de Oakland una pequeña Motown independiente: «¿para qué queremos los sellos?». Ritmos lentos con el bajo grave, hechos para el coche; sellos como Sick Wid’ It de E-40, Strictly Business de The Mac y Mac Dre o Get Low de JT the Bigga Figga: «hicimos nosotros la industria».

refs.q: Everybody growing up in Oakland has some type of hustler’s mentality.
refs.para: Ant Banks (producer, Dangerous Crew): Everybody growing up in Oakland has some type of hustler’s mentality.

refs.q: I felt like I saw the future of rap and his name was Too $hort.
refs.para: The minute I heard “Freaky Tales” I was like, I’m fucking sold. It’s almost like Jon Landau said he saw the future of rock and roll: His name was Bruce Springsteen. I felt like I saw the future of rap and his name was Too $hort. And it was nasty, dirty, and everybody at RCA Records rebelled. There were pressing plants that rebelled. I was like, “Fuck it, go find another pressing plant because this shit’s coming out.” And we went with it, and it was just explosive, and it did exactly what I thought and hoped that it would do. It started to break in the South—Louisiana, Mississippi—with heavy 808, heavy bassline. No radio play and a platinum album.

refs.q: Because we didn’t have the actual labels here in the Bay Area, we made the industry.
refs.para: Mac Mall (artist, Bay Area): Strictly Business Records was the label of The Mac and Mac Dre. They were independent. [E-40’s] Sick Wid’ It, independent company. JT the Bigga Figga, Get Low [Recordz]. 75 Girls from Too $hort was an independent company before he signed to Jive. Because we didn’t have the actual labels here in the Bay Area, we made the industry.

refs.q: You can’t really do nothing too fast there but drive.
refs.para: What people don’t understand about Oakland is we are a slow-moving little city. You can’t really do nothing too fast there but drive. So, regardless to what kind of music was out, or however it sound, only thing that matters is what does it sound like in the car?
